history.station: RAF Kirmington, Lincolnshire (sole WW2 operational base)
history.summary: No. 166 Squadron RAF was re-formed on 27 January 1943 at RAF Kirmington, Lincolnshire, and flew from that single base for the entire war. The squadron began operations on Wellington bombers in January 1943 before converting to the Avro Lancaster in September 1943. In two years of operations, the squadron flew 5,061 sorties against 255 targets in enemy and occupied countries, dropping 24,022 tons of high explosive, 3,429 tons of incendiaries, and laying 701 tons of sea mines. 178 aircraft were lost — 51 Wellingtons and 127 Lancasters — and 921 aircrew were killed. The primary memorial to the squadron stands in the village of Kirmington itself, with a Lancaster propeller blade on a plinth erected on 3 September 1988.

notable_personnel.name: RAF Kirmington & 166 Squadron Aircrew
notable_personnel.detail: The squadron's Roll of Honour records 921 aircrew killed — one of the highest losses of any single Lancaster squadron in Bomber Command. A searchable personnel database is maintained by the 166 Squadron Association at raf166squadron.com.
